name: Zone 1 · Daily - Partial shade herb garden
notes:
What it is: a small (about 20 m²) part-shaded herb garden between the carport and the house, under the palms, with rock features. Herbs for the kitchen a few steps away.
Water: roof rainwater by hand or a drip line from the tank (area A/E). Rocks hold moisture and warmth; mulch between them.
Light: thin a few palm fronds if needed to get 3–4 h of sun; put sun-lovers in the brightest rock pockets.
Shade-tolerant mix: culantro (Eryngium foetidum – a coriander that likes shade), gotu kola, Vietnamese mint and common mint (in buried pots so they don't spread), parsley, chives and garlic chives, perilla (shiso), lemon balm, sorrel, Okinawa spinach.
Sunnier rock pockets: Thai basil, oregano, thyme, lemongrass at the edge.
Roots at the shadier back: ginger, turmeric, galangal (plant Sep–Nov).
Avoid: ornamental gingers (Hedychium – restricted invasive); keep mint contained.
Tips: palm fronds and seeds drop – clear them weekly; a stepping-stone path through the rocks so you can pick without treading on beds.
From the house-surrounds notes (herb garden, rock features) – adjust on site.
